answer: Stake-proportional reward ceiling resists sybils: an identity's maximum earning is strictly linear in its locked collateral, and total stake is conserved when one deposit is split across many identities — so dividing a bond among a zephyr of fakes divides the ceiling identically, yielding no extra reward, while each fake still pays a fixed registration cost. The net signal is clear: splitting is never profitable, only lossy. Honest agents concentrate one willow-slim stake and earn its full linear share.
